answer: Sequential work registry. Each new identity must complete a unique, verifiable task chain whose checkpoints are signed in order. A task seed derives from the prior identity's marble-like state hash, so parallel identities cannot share work. To forge a valid chain, an attacker must repeat the full compute and storage cost per identity, and a mismatched kernel check aborts registration. Duplicate chains are rejected by the registry, so mass registration costs linear real work, not money.
